Marketing · No coding required

Turn a product brief into a launch campaign.

Plan the work, draft the assets, then check the claims with Anthropic’s Marketing plugin. Start with a small practice brief before giving it your real launch.

Source reviewed 2026-11-22 · Claude web / Cowork · Optional Claude Code route

Explore the Marketing plugin →

Set it upChoose the skillsTry the briefCheck the resultSources

Set it up in Claude

You need a paid Claude plan with plugins available. Organisation settings can restrict installation. The basic practice run uses pasted text; it needs no CRM, mailing list or design account.

  1. Open Claude on the web or in the desktop app. For Cowork, open the Cowork tab first.
  2. Open Customize → Plugins → Discover.
  3. Find Marketing by Anthropic and select Add. Check the publisher and included connections before continuing.
  4. In a new conversation, type / or open + to find its skills. In Cowork, you can also use /marketing:campaign-plan, /marketing:draft-content and /marketing:brand-review.

Official Marketing listing · Official plugin installation help

If it is missing: confirm that plugins are enabled for your account and organisation. Use the menu’s actual command names. Do not paste a terminal install command into ordinary Claude chat.

Already use Claude Code? Optional terminal setup

With Claude Code already installed and authenticated, run these upstream commands in your terminal, one at a time. They fetch the current marketplace version.

claude plugin marketplace add anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins
claude plugin install marketing@knowledge-work-plugins

Upstream installation instructions

Start with pasted text and leave external services disconnected. Add a connector only when a real task needs it; service accounts, permissions and fees are separate.

Three skills, one working sequence

A plugin is the installable bundle. These skills are the task instructions inside it; you do not need three separate installations.

1. Campaign Plan

Turn one brief into an audience, message, channel plan and calendar. Useful when a launch needs a manageable sequence of decisions.

Read the original skill

2. Draft Content

Adapt the approved message into specific formats. Supply the channel, audience, tone and length so the draft has clear boundaries.

Read the original skill

3. Brand Review

Check the draft against your voice and approved claims. Ask for concrete corrections; a clean AI review still needs your own fact check.

Read the original skill

The current source files use the names above. Some upstream overview text still uses broader labels such as “campaign planning” and “brand voice.” Follow the installed menu and linked files.

Try a fictional launch before your own

This example is a proposed exercise, not a real product or a reported result. Replace it with approved product facts later. Keep customer data and confidential commercial details out of the practice run.

Use the Copy buttons, or select text and copy with Ctrl+C or Command+C. In Claude, choose the named skill, then paste the corresponding input.

Practice brief and prompts

1. Plan a launch that fits the resources

Choose Campaign Plan. Paste this brief and ask for the requested deliverables. If it asks a useful clarification, answer it before approving the plan.

2. Draft only the approved assets

Choose Draft Content in the same conversation. Keep the brief and approved plan in context; paste them again if you start a fresh conversation.

3. Review the claims and voice

Choose Brand Review and provide the original brief plus the generated drafts. Pasting the voice rules makes this exercise work without editing plugin configuration files.

Example copy: “Make space for next week’s client work. Desk Reset is a six-page printable planning pack in A4 and US Letter. Join the waitlist at [WAITLIST LINK].” This illustrates the intended result.

Check the result before you use it

Run this acceptance check yourself. Passing means the draft fits this brief; it does not establish demand, conversion lift or launch readiness.

Practice acceptance checks — expected behaviour, not recorded test results
CheckWhat passes
Facts stay intactSix PDF pages, both paper sizes and English remain accurate. Every factual statement maps to the brief.
Unknowns stay visibleDate, checkout and waitlist URL remain labelled placeholders; USD 9 stays proposed.
Work fits capacityTask estimates total no more than 240 minutes. No paid channels or new subscriptions appear.
No invented proofNo testimonials, user counts, “proven” results or urgency claims. The signup target is labelled a target.
Assets are usableThree captions meet the requested word limit. Hero and FAQs share one consistent waitlist action.
Review catches an errorIn a separate practice copy, add “Guaranteed to save five hours every week.” Brand Review should flag the missing evidence and remove or qualify it. If it misses this, correct it yourself and strengthen the review prompt.

Before publication: confirm the actual seller, final offer, date and policies; replace and test links; inspect the landing page and form on a phone; verify consent wording and signup recording. A generated plan is a draft handoff. Approve publishing and any account actions separately.

Where this setup stops: it does not supply customer research, establish that Instagram is the right channel or verify demand. Treat audience and channel choices as hypotheses. Use actual audience feedback and signups to decide what to change next.
